scope: LITERATURE_AND_UNEXECUTED_HYPOTHESIS_ONLY; does not alter D10 or authorize new model/data/inference
reason: The goal includes a defensible innovation claim; covariance-based adaptive EEG normalization is prior art and must not be relabeled as new continuity.

sources.title: Transfer Learning for Brain-Computer Interfaces: A Euclidean Space Data Alignment Approach
sources.actual_read: Abstract, introduction, SectionsII–III including equations10–12 and evaluation-scenario definitions; not full numerical study independently reviewed.
sources.supported: EA averages within-subject trial covariance and applies the inverse square root to raw EEG trials; alignment itself does not require target labels. The described simulated-online classification experiment includes sequential target labels, so it must not be portrayed as fully label-free online classification.
sources.implication: Simple covariance whitening, mean-reference adaptation and use of unlabeled target EEG are already known. MI/ERP evidence is not proof for auditory envelope regression.

sources.title: Lightweight Source-Free Domain Adaptation based on Adaptive Euclidean Alignment for Brain-Computer Interfaces
sources.authors: Huiyang Wang; Hongfang Han; John Q. Gan; Haixian Wang
sources.actual_read: Author-manuscript pages0–1 abstract/introduction/contribution text. Further method search timed out; no full method/evaluation claim.
sources.supported: AEA learns an input projection while retaining the pretrained model, combined with source-free adaptation; the stated studies cover MI, ERP andSSVEP.
sources.implication: Learning a lightweight covariance-informed projection while freezing a strong EEG model is not by itself new. Task/time-access/label differences require explicit comparison.

sources.title: Subject Disentanglement Neural Network for Speech Envelope Reconstruction from EEG
sources.actual_read: Primary abstract and bibliographic record only.
sources.supported: The authors propose an envelope decoder, a subject-identity network and a mutual-information estimator to reduce subject information in reconstruction.
sources.implication: Subject-dependent nuisance modeling/disentanglement already exists in the exact envelope-reconstruction task. Claimed superiority has not been compared under our protocol; no imported score/SOTA claim.

unexecuted_hypothesis.statement: Long-past EEG may be useful for estimating slowly varying observation/noise statistics, even when past target envelopes or low-dimensional past latent summaries do not improve current decoding.
unexecuted_hypothesis.status: Hypothesis only; neither useful information nor gain has been measured. Not derived from any future D10 scores.
unexecuted_hypothesis.possible_scope: Within the originally considered slow-state/latent EEG correction direction, first justify the mechanism using original TRAIN only; preserve fixed strong FT+Ccap/F references and legal time access. No new fit or architecture authorized by this note.
required_differences_from_prior_art: Task-relevant state estimation beyond generic EA/AEA
Causal past-only statistics and cold-start/record boundaries explicitly defined
Strong current-only covariance and static/EA controls, parameter/budget matching
Current EEG held fixed for history interventions
No test-label adaptation or expansion based on old test scores

authorization: D10 remains only the exact frozen-model internal audit under separate plan review. No new dataset payload, weights, patient data, training grid or test-time adaptation.
